The numerical libraries are installable declarations, the classifier is a pinned project component installed locally, and orchestration tools are explicitly required. The equivalent-evidence rule permits this split between image dependencies and documented host orchestration; vendoring all package dependencies is unnecessary.

The frozen Git inventory and commit history identify source, manuscript, configuration and module revisions. Omitted capture payloads do not negate original Git tracking. This verdict is supported independently of checkout cleanliness.

The image layer paths have annex content keys in the frozen inventory, and the gaze dataset explains its Git-plus-annex storage. These directly establish large-content versioning without pretending the unavailable layer or data bytes were inspected.

The root provides tool installation links and explicit commands for numerical replay and PDF construction. Old instructions are openly distinguished from the replacement route, so the method forbids treating those two accounts alone as a silent conflict. No make changes target is promised.

Root data selection uses relative joins. The linked submit generator embeds a specific home directory and Python executable, giving a specific counterexample within the wider inspected boundary. Container-internal paths and Windows prompt examples should not be counted as host-path violations.

The direct numerical imports and imported classifier/helper dependencies map to declared NumPy, SciPy, statsmodels, matplotlib/pylab, pandas, seaborn and scikit-learn. The DataLad import has an explicit fallback, with inputs provisioned by the outer run. Make, Inkscape and TeX tools are declared. This supports completeness of the documented final-analysis route; it is not proof of rebuilding success.

The README identifies tested operating systems, Docker and tool versions, but the adapter expressly assumes non-root Docker management and the linked legacy submission route assumes a particular working directory and inherited environment. Partial is supported by concrete configuration assumptions, not merely a generic desire for more documentation.

Host prerequisites and numerical/typesetting package lists are present and readable along the main route. This is a requirements-list property; the known legacy host assumptions are appropriately distinguished under must/011.

The frozen Git tree includes the recipe, registered invocation and image identity metadata beside code. This directly establishes tracked environment specifications and does not depend on image download or successful execution.

History supplies runnable build/save commands and a later recorded format-maintenance operation. The dependency-change history also records adding scikit-learn for the added kappa computation. Together these support a practiced, tracked maintenance route. The first image build alone would only establish initial creation, so the later maintenance evidence is essential.

The image has explicit SHA256 descriptors and config/layer identities. The adapter hashes the archived config and executes the resulting image ID; latest is a preserved tag annotation, not evidence of a registry pull during replay. Exact byte retrieval remains unverified, but identification is supported.

The annex metadata records an image-blob URL, and published specifications are represented in the corpus. Neither supplies an independent recipient retrieval of the exact current payload. Not-checked follows the native publication rule and cohort prohibition; absent capture payloads are not retrieval failures.

The root explains how to install prerequisites, clone, replay and build the manuscript, and the named docker-make registration exists. This is evidence of obtaining/using instructions, while actual availability and broader historical label-environment reconstruction remain separate issues.

Root and discovered data/software modules share Git revision links, with DataLad/git-annex extending the same framework for large files. No separate incompatible version-control scheme is visible in the inspected components.

There is completed manual numerical recomputation and later archive maintenance, plus classifier testing infrastructure. These are useful but limited evidence of ongoing accuracy of the full instructions; the linked labels README still names removed scripts. Partial is more defensible than either a full pass from CI presence or failure based solely on missing root CI.

Raw inputs, labels and classifier have separate repositories; analysis, figures and environment also have distinct locations. The root consumes the derivative module rather than mixing label-generation changes into raw data, supporting the modular-separation property.

The inspected required data are described as unrestricted and runtime software has open distribution terms. No restricted required component was identified, so the empty-subject N/A is appropriately qualified. Lack of payload access in this inspection is not itself an access restriction.

The completed Docker analysis is valid historical fresh-container evidence for the final summaries and figures. It consumes previously generated label TSVs; it does not execute the linked label-generation pipeline. The assessment includes that component for provenance and portability defects but does not explain why its unverified fresh-environment testing is excluded from this full met verdict.

Readers can navigate the top-level links and commands, but the linked labels reproduction document leads to obsolete script names. The presence of machine-readable module paths supports partial navigation assistance, without erasing that documented dead end.
